snippet.title: Is a Star Really Coming Towards Us?
snippet.description:
What Happens When a Star Passes Through Our Solar System?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-jImX5h7ws

In the constellation Serpens, the orange dwarf star Gliese 710 is heading nearly straight towards our Solar System at about 51,000 kilometres an hour. In roughly 1.3 million years, it will sail right through the outer edge of the Solar System — the icy shell of the Oort Cloud.

Sources: Bailer-Jones (2022), The Astrophysical Journal Letters 935 L9 — Gaia DR3 encounter distance, velocity, and timing (https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac816a) · Berski & Dybczyński (2016), Astronomy & Astrophysics 595 L10 — Gliese 710 flyby and Oort Cloud encounter (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201629835) · NASA Science, Oort Cloud Facts — the distant comet reservoir (https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/oort-cloud/facts/).

Pictures: ESA/Gaia/DPAC proper-motion starfield sweep across 1.6 million years and ESA/Gaia/DPAC EDR3 all-sky Milky Way star map (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO), alongside original animated explainers and AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: ESA/Gaia/DPAC (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/igo/).
